messages:
morgan: Morning — woke up to three advisories: etcd (high/remote), cert-manager (priv esc-ish), and nginx-ingress (moderate). We need triage, patch schedule, and to confirm any RBAC/KMS/audit impacts. Who can own inventory and rollout plan?

anita: TL;DR from initial read: etcd CVE-2026-1234 looks highest impact (RCE via gRPC path, CVSS ~9.0). cert-manager CVE-2026-2345 is lower (privilege escalation via chain validation bug) — patch available 1.11.4. nginx-ingress CVE-2026-3456 is moderate (path traversal) but widely exploitable on external entrypoints.

sam: I can run a cluster inventory and list affected versions. Will check control planes and managed clusters. Running quick checks now: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l app=etcd` (note: etcd is static pod on masters so may need direct node checks). Posting a results snippet shortly.

cve-bot: Advisory posted: CVE-2026-1234 (etcd) — https://advisories.example/CVE-2026-1234 — exploitability: remote unauthenticated? note says depends on cluster config.

lina: KMS/audit note: if we upgrade cert-manager it will touch Secrets (controller reissues), but we do NOT need to rotate KMS keys unless a key compromise is indicated. Rewrapping encryption at rest (EncryptionConfiguration) with a new key requires re-encrypting resources — that's a separate maintenance task; avoid during emergency patch unless absolutely needed. Also ensure audit policy is capturing `authentication`, `authorization`, and `secrets` write events before we roll.

raja: RBAC: cert-manager change might need a small ClusterRole tweak for new controllers. I drafted a minimal change to let the backup operator continue to list/watch CertificateRequests and Secrets without broad privileges. Example snippet:```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: backup-operator-certmgr
rules:
- apiGroups: ["cert-manager.io"]
  resources: ["certificates","certificaterequests"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch"]
- apiGroups: ["" ]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get","list"]
```
I'll open a PR after we decide rollout cadence.

morgan: Good. Sam — can you confirm which clusters run vulnerable etcd (image tags), and whether any control planes are publicly routable? That determines urgency. ops-oncall: are we okay with a late-night canary?

ops-oncall: We can do a canary tonight 22:00 UTC for non-customer-facing clusters (staging, canary). Production windows: prefer 02:00–06:00 UTC with 1-hour waves so we can detect issues. For etcd specifically, we need snapshot-before + verify restore plan.

sam: Inventory quick results (summary):
- prod-control-1/2/3: etcd:3.5.9 (vulnerable per advisory)
- staging-control-1: etcd:3.5.11 (patched)
- managed-k8s (partner): etcd:3.4.x (old; needs separate coord)
So yes — production control planes are impacted.

manual: recommended immediate actions:
1) Preflight: take etcd snapshot (s3), verify checksum.
2) Canary: patch a single control-plane in canary cluster (drain if required, restart static pod).
3) Monitor: etcd metrics, API latency, control-plane errors for 30m.
4) Roll waves: 1 master at a time with 15-min stabilization between nodes.
5) Rollback: have snapshot restore doc open and ops person ready.

lina: Monitoring & audit checklist before patch: ensure audit logs retained for 30d for high-sensitivity clusters, enable verbose etcd logging for canary during the window, and re-run our decrypt test against KMS after upgrade (to confirm no regression).

raja: RBAC PR: I'll make the role tweak non-breaking and bind to `system:serviceaccount:backup:operator` only. No need to widen system:masters.

morgan: cert-manager plan: upgrade to 1.11.4 in canary tonight after etcd canary ok. Use helm upgrade with `--atomic --timeout 10m`. Commands:```bash
helm upgrade cert-manager jetstack/cert-manager \
  --namespace cert-manager \
  --version 1.11.4 \
  --set installCRDs=true \
  --atomic --timeout 10m
```
Watch certs and CertificateRequest queue.

sam: nginx-ingress: low priority but public-facing — schedule with next regular edge patch (7 days) unless we see PoC. I'll lock rule to deny exploit patterns at edge WAF as temporary mitigation.

deploy-bot: Planned rollout created: canary=2026-06-12T22:00Z, prod-wave-1=2026-06-13T02:00Z, prod-wave-2=2026-06-13T03:00Z, prod-wave-3=2026-06-13T04:00Z. See: https://deploys.local/rollouts/1797554321

anita: Approve the plan. Two asks before we start: (1) Ensure kube-apiserver audit policy includes `secrets` write events; (2) Backups validated and quick restore runbook posted in thread.

raja: posted PR draft for RBAC: https://git.local/rbac/PR-432 — small role + binding, tests included.

ops-oncall: I'll be on-call during the window. If etcd shows high election churn, abort and roll back to snapshot.

morgan: Great. Owners: Sam = inventory & patch agent, Raja = RBAC PR, Lina = KMS/audit checks, Ops-oncall = on-call and snapshot restore. Action items in issue: https://issues.local/SEC-789. If nobody objects, we'll run canary tonight. :thumbsup:
